newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks edge up on back of selected scrips.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks edge up on back of selected scrips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly higher on Monday on foreign buying of blue chips and plantation shares, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.21 points up at 629.80. Blue chips John Keells Holdings Ltd rose four rupees to 198, Hayleys Ltd 4.50 to 201.
Turnover, led by foreign buying, was 73.3 million rupees. The main trade was 100,000 John Keells Holdings.
"We had the buy order for John Keells for some time but could not source it without paying a premium," said Rohan Fernando, a trader at CT Smith Stock Brokers.
A regional fund and a plantation investment fund were active on Monday, brokers said.
"With many finance sector stocks and all the plantation firms having done well in 1996, the two areas are being favoured," said a broker who declined to be identified.
Local investors, at one point waiting to see if violence ahead of March 21 local government elections would move prices, were refocusing on the market, brokers said.
Better-than-anticipated 1996 results were acting as an inducement to bring investors back, they said.
